newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures took their cue from weaker US Treasuries and German bunds to end the day lower, after dropping through several key support levels, and dealers said further weakness was on the cards given the worries about German monetary policy.

Short-covering after Friday's sell-off did lift the September bond future off its low of 129.68 mid-afternoon, but the contract dropped through support at 129.80 just before the close. Next support is seen between 129.64 and 129.68.

All eyes now are on the Bundesbank, which could signal a change to a variable rate repo as early as tomorrow in a bid to shore up the shaky mark and preempt import inflation. Such a move would open the way towards higher interest rates.

Analysts were divided about whether the German central bank would actually signal a change. Some argued that the weakness of the German economy, with its high unemployment rate, militated against any sign of tightbe found in the forex markets.

" I think a change is possible. The dollar keeps going higher, there is no end in sight," said a trader at a French brokerage house. He said that if the Bundesbank changed to a variable rate repo, September PIBOR could go as low as 96.20-96.30. But he thought the downside on the September future was limited.
PIBOR was off four basis points at the close on Monday at 96.43, leaving implied three-month interest rates at 3.57 percent compared with 3.37 on the cash market.
